summary: Deschutes NF Cabin Lake guard station: ranger station HQ 1921-45, CCC camp 1934-38 (Wikipedia credits it with the existing buildings; the NRHP nomination dates two of them to 1923), NRHP 1986, closed 2002. A water-tank lookout claim appears only in the Oregon list.

access.note: The guard station is closed; the adjacent campground is open. The dirt road to the station can be rough.

events.note: Headquarters of the Fort Rock Ranger District from 1921 until 1945, with five full-time rangers living there for most of that time
The NRHP nomination dates the bunkhouse and generator house to 1923

A CCC camp stood beside the station (1934 to 1938). Wikipedia credits CCC crews with the existing guard station buildings, but the nomination dates the bunkhouse and generator house to 1923 and the cookhouse to 1934
Headquarters moved to Bend and the ranger station was converted to a guard station, used as a bunkhouse and supply base for fire crews
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places, reference number 86000827
The Forest Service closed the guard station

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Oregon list describes a water tank tower used as an emergency lookout. The Wikipedia history and the NRHP nomination describe a ranger station and guard station compound, and neither describes a tower or tank. The story reports the list's claim as unconfirmed.
Wikipedia says CCC crews built the existing guard station buildings in 1934 to 1938, but the NRHP nomination dates the bunkhouse and generator house to 1923, so those two predate the CCC camp.

notes_for_editor: The brief had no lookout facts. The only tower claim is the Oregon list's water tank tower, and no source read confirms it, so kind stays unknown. The NRHP nomination text read had no lookout, tower or tank lines. The Living New Deal page returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Wikipedia says six of seven CCC-built structures remain; a Bend Bulletin count of eight was not verified. Wildlife guzzlers and watering holes mentioned in 2025 bird-group notes were not used as a lookout. Status of any tank or tower is unknown; the Deschutes NF Fort Rock or Bend district heritage staff could confirm it. Coordinates in the brief match Wikipedia (43.49056, -121.05861).
